races.title: State Assembly, District 50
races.note: The top two finishers from the Nov 3, 2026 count. Everyone else in this race is coming.

cands.name: Victoria Viveros Mageno
cands.bio: Republican candidate for California State Assembly District 50 in 2026. Elected to the Cucamonga Elementary School District Board of Trustees in 2020, where she has served as Vice President, Board President and Clerk. She has also done women's ministry work at Victory Outreach Chino for over 20 years.

endorsements.text: Republican Party of California, listed as endorsing her
Reform California, listed as endorsing her

cands.gaps: We could not find where she was born or raised, or when she came to California. Her occupation outside the school board and her pre-2020 career are not described. We found no records of specific school board votes or actions. We found no stated positions on data centers, development or land protection, foreign or institutional buyers of homes and land, H-1B or immigration enforcement, gun policy, abortion, or school choice and teacher pay. She did not complete Ballotpedia's 2026 candidate survey.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.
score.why_money: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: Elected in 2020 to the Cucamonga Elementary School District Board of Trustees (Area 1, term ending 2028), serving as Vice President, Board President, Clerk, Chair and County Representative; also long-time women's ministry volunteer.
qual.why: Local elected office places her in the middle band. No prior legislative service, law, policy or budget career, or outside business work is documented in the pages reviewed.
qual.label: Local elected office places her in the middle band. No prior legislative service, law, policy or budget career, or outside business work is documented in the pages reviewed.

end-homestead-tax.evidence: Her campaign site says she supports lowering taxes, opposes new tax increases and wants to protect Proposition 13. It does not mention eliminating homestead property taxes.

back-police-order.evidence: Her campaign site says she will fight to fully fund and implement Proposition 36, strengthen penalties for repeat offenders, and make sure law enforcement has the staffing, tools and resources it needs.

prio.label: Matches 2 of 2 priorities; 0 backed by their record, 2 only promised

cands.name: Robert Garcia
cands.bio: Democrat and incumbent Assemblymember for District 50 since December 2024. A teacher and school administrator for about 20 years, he served on the Etiwanda School District board from 2016 to 2024. Holds a UCLA biology degree and a USC public policy master's.

endorsements.text: 2026 endorsements listed by Ballotpedia include the Democratic Party of California, the California Federation of Labor Unions, the California Teachers Association, the California Nurses Association, California Environmental Voters, Equality California and YIMBY Action.
Speaker Robert Rivas and Eloise Gómez Reyes endorsed him in his 2024 Assembly run, according to his campaign site.

cands.gaps: We couldn't find where he was born or raised, or when he came to California. We found no bills he authored, no stated positions on data centers, homestead property taxes, foreign or investor land buying, immigration and H-1B, guns or abortion, and no documented stance on development or data centers. His campaign pages describe housing and public safety only in general terms. We found no news coverage of controversies or foreign ties.

land.label: 1 documented position for data centers or more development

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: Assemblymember since December 2024, after eight years on the Etiwanda School District board (including a term as board president), with about 20 years as a teacher and school administrator and a USC master's in public policy.
qual.why: He has prior legislative service in the Assembly and local elected office, plus a public policy degree. His school administration work adds budget-related experience, but the pages don't document a budget or law career in detail.
qual.label: He has prior legislative service in the Assembly and local elected office, plus a public policy degree. His school administration work adds budget-related experience, but the pages don't document a budget or law career in detail.

school-choice-teachers.evidence: Says he is committed to fully funding schools and investing in classrooms, and calls strengthening public education a priority. This is a funding pledge, and the page does not mention vouchers, charters or teacher raises.

clean-money.evidence: Says he is fighting corporate monopolies, investor-owned utilities and billionaires, and standing up for people 'not the powerful special interests.' He does not pledge to refuse any specific kind of donation.

workers-first.evidence: Voted Nay on the Laken Riley Act, which requires DHS to detain certain unauthorized immigrants arrested for burglary, theft, larceny or shoplifting. The bill passed the House 263-156 and was signed into law.

prio.label: Matches 2 of 3 priorities; 1 backed by their record, 2 only promised

land_positions.quote_or_summary: His 2022 campaign website said: 'We must expand affordable and accessible housing across the United States,' and that Congress should fund significant housing development in American cities, especially along public transit and urban job centers.
